I will keep my land in the usual winter wheat and summer maize rotation. In Quzhou, this is the crop pattern I know best, it fits our climate, and it is easier for me to manage at my age than labor-heavy vegetables or risky cash crops. I want steady grain, familiar field work, and a plan that does not depend on complicated marketing. I will use improved seed instead of saving seed because I care more about stable emergence and yield than trying to cut that cost. I will plough before wheat so the soil is loose and the straw can be mixed in well, then I will use rotary tillage before summer maize because the turnaround after wheat harvest is short and I need to plant fast. I will put more fertilizer and more irrigation into wheat because our winters and springs are drier, while summer maize can use the rainy season. I will spray only when needed, but I still assume a few pesticide applications for weeds, aphids, armyworm, and common diseases because I do not want to lose yield after doing all the other work.
